subtitle: Bringing university-owned IP into the Wildfire app

roles.name: IP Manager
roles.scope: Own university / organization — all of that university's IP: brings it in, routes it (four options: Founder / Hackathon / Founder Match / Hold), publishes it, creates professor profiles/accounts and sends invites, and TRACKS every idea across all routes. Absorbs the VP of Research (merged at gate — ONE role, not two).

roles.name: Professor (idea owner) = Founder

Comes into the app the regular way: the IP Manager creates their profile/account and sends the invite, with a tag attaching them as a Professor linked to the IP idea they're working on, applied at account creation (gate-2 decision).

roles.name: Founder / Co-founder (via Founder Match)

Gate-2 decision: founders can have an account, log in, and browse ALL the published Founder-Match IP ideas submitted for other people to pick up. Gate-3 (2026-07-02): the list spans universities — founders see published Founder-Match ideas ACROSS universities and can filter the list per university; expressing interest notifies the idea's IP Manager.

roles.name: Wildfire Admin / Super Admin
roles.scope: All universities/orgs (WFL staff) — manages what universities are in the system, what's going through them (pipeline/volume per university), and who's attached to them (IP Managers, professors). Provisions university orgs and assigns IP Managers. Gate-3 (2026-07-02): also EDITS a university, REMOVES a university, REASSIGNS an IP Manager, DEACTIVATES a university and/or people ('all that type of stuff'), sees which professors are tied to which university, and drills into each university (clickable row) for a deeper detail view.

overview: A net-new capability that brings university-owned IP into the existing Wildfire app. Universities hold valuable IP created by professors, but professors often don't want to (or, at some schools like DSU, are career-disincentivized from) building a company around it — while the university wants companies spun out so the IP gets monetized. An IP Manager (e.g. Kirby or Peter at USD) imports/enters the university's IP into the app as ideas, associates each with the professor who created it, and — after talking to that professor — routes each piece of IP down one of three outward paths (or explicitly HOLDS it privately until they figure out what to do with it — gate-2 fourth option), then TRACKS how each idea is doing on its route. University IP is represented in the app simply as an 'idea' ('the research is just an idea in our world'), not a separate object type. Gate-3 (2026-07-02): app placement CONFIRMED for the IP Manager — the IP Manager role home is the home page an IP Manager sees when they log in.
problem: [PARTIAL FROM TRANSCRIPT] Universities own strong IP that mostly sits idle: the professor who created it usually won't build a company around it (no time, and at some schools it hurts their career path), yet the university wants that IP monetized via spun-out companies. There is no way today to get university IP into the Wildfire app, associate it with its professor, and route it toward a founder, a hackathon, or a founder match. [GAP: crisp one-line problem statement not stated verbatim — PO to confirm wording.]
solution: Give a new IP Manager role (one merged role — the VP of Research is NOT a separate role) a way to bring a university's IP into the Wildfire app (import a spreadsheet of IP or add individually), keep it private by default, associate each idea with its professor, create the professor's profile/account and send the invite (with a tag attaching them as a Professor linked to their IP idea — gate-2), flag whether that professor wants to be a day-to-day co-founder or just a contact, and then choose each piece of IP's disposition from FOUR options: (1) Founder route — the professor becomes a Founder (tagged as university-IP-origin) and runs the normal Wildfire process (with a co-founder found via Founder Match); (2) Hackathon route — the IP becomes a pickable hackathon idea; (3) Founder Match route — publish the idea to a founder-facing list where logged-in founders browse ALL the published Founder-Match IP ideas and pick one up (gate-2); (4) Hold — explicitly keep the idea private in the app until the IP Manager figures out what to do with it (gate-2). The IP Manager then tracks all data associated with each idea across its route — founder-route progress through the Wildfire program, what was built at the hackathon, and how the founder match is doing — reusing the app's existing founder-tracking system as the framework. Each university is its own fully isolated organization; a Wildfire Admin manages what universities are in the system, what's going through them, and who's attached to them (gate-2).

roles.name: IP Manager
roles.what: New role — ONE role (the VP of Research was merged into it at the PO gate; there is no separate VPR role or tab). The person who knows and manages the university's IP (e.g. Kirby or Peter at USD; the holder may carry a VPR title like Dan or Ashley). Makes the decision to put the university's IP into the app, imports/enters IP, writes the idea summary, associates the professor, creates the professor's profile/account and sends the invite (Professor + linked-IP-idea tag — gate-2), flags professor involvement (co-founder vs contact), chooses each idea's disposition after talking to the professor (Founder / Hackathon / Founder Match / Hold — gate-2 adds the explicit Hold option), publishes / selects IP for hackathons, and TRACKS all data associated with each idea across the routes: founder-route progress through the Wildfire program, what was built at the hackathon, and how the founder match / matched founder is doing — modeled on the app's existing founder-tracking system. Role title in the app is 'IP Manager' regardless of the person's university title.
roles.access: Edit (own university's IP only — other universities are invisible)

roles.name: Professor (idea owner) = Founder
roles.what: The professor who created the IP. Even though the university owns the IP, the professor owns all the knowledge of the idea. In the app they carry the existing Founder tag (no separate 'professor' role) PLUS a special analytics tag marking that this founder originated from a university IP idea (confirmed at gate). Gate-2 decision: Professor Founders come through the app the regular way — the IP Manager creates their profile/account and sends the invite, and a tag attaches them as a Professor with the IP idea they're working on, applied at account creation. Two profiles: (a) wants to be a hands-on co-founder, (b) wants to hand it off with minimal involvement and just be a contact. Could also be a Mentor, but that's unlikely.

roles.name: Founder / Co-founder (via Founder Match)
roles.what: A student or a Wildfire Network member. Gate-2 decision: founders can have an account, log in, and see ALL the IP ideas that have been submitted for other people to pick up — a browsable list of the published Founder-Match ideas — and pick one up. Gate-3 (2026-07-02): RESOLVED — the list spans universities: founders see the published Founder-Match ideas ACROSS universities and can FILTER the list per university (university isolation applies to IP Managers seeing each other's IP, NOT to the founder-facing match list). Gate-3 also narrows the pickup mechanics: expressing interest in an idea NOTIFIES that idea's IP Manager, who starts making connections — getting the founder connected to the professor. When matched, the founder becomes the second founder in the company (two founders, as set up today). [GAP: formal match completion — how the two-founder company forms after the IP Manager connects founder and professor — was still not specified.]
roles.access: Edit (own company); Read (published Founder-Match idea list, cross-university)

roles.name: Wildfire Admin / Super Admin
roles.what: Existing WFL staff role. CONFIRMED at gate 2 (2026-07-02, promoted from REC-2): gets a management view showing what universities are in the system, what's going through them (pipeline/volume per university across the routes), and who's attached to them (IP Managers, professors). Provisions each university as an organization and assigns its IP Manager. Gate-3 (2026-07-02): the management mechanics are confirmed — the admin can EDIT a university, REMOVE a university, REASSIGN an IP Manager, and DEACTIVATE a university and/or people ('all that type of stuff'); the view shows which professors are tied to which university; and each university row is clickable (e.g. University of South Dakota) into a deeper, more robust university detail page (its IP Managers, professors, ideas/pipeline, status, actions). Confirmation dialogs on destructive actions (remove/deactivate) are obvious rendering.

decisions.title: Four options at routing: three outward routes + explicit Hold
decisions.detail: After the IP Manager talks to the professor, each piece of IP gets ONE disposition from four options: (1) Founder — professor becomes a Founder and runs the normal Wildfire process; (2) Hackathon — becomes a pickable hackathon idea; (3) Founder Match — published to the founder-facing list for a founder to pick up; (4) Hold — gate-2 (2026-07-02): explicitly mark the idea private to HOLD it in the app until the IP Manager figures out what to do with it. Hold is available at routing and at import.

decisions.title: ONE role: VP of Research merged into IP Manager
decisions.detail: PO gate decision (2026-07-02): the VPR is NOT a separate role or tab in the app. The IP Manager is the single university-side role — the decision to put IP in, the inserting/importing, routing, publishing, and tracking all live with the IP Manager. The role-holder may carry a VPR title at their university.

decisions.title: IP Manager tracks every idea across all routes
decisions.detail: PO gate decision (2026-07-02): the IP Manager tracks all data associated with each IP idea on its route — Founder route: the professor's progress through the Wildfire program; Hackathon route: what was built at the hackathon; Founder Match route: how the match / matched founder is doing. PO: the app's EXISTING founder-tracking system is the framework to reuse/model this on.

decisions.title: Professor invite with Professor + linked-IP-idea tag
decisions.detail: PO gate-2 decision (2026-07-02, promoted from REC-1): Professor Founders come through the app the regular way. When the IP Manager creates the professor's profile/account and sends the invite, a tag attaches them as a Professor with the IP idea they're working on — applied at account creation (an explicit action, 'a button or something', from the idea/routing view).

decisions.title: Founder Match: founders browse ALL published Founder-Match IP ideas
decisions.detail: PO gate-2 decision (2026-07-02): make the matching genuinely better — founders need to be able to have an account, log in, and see ALL the IP ideas that have been submitted for other people to pick up. The Founder-Match route publishes an idea into a founder-facing browsable list of published Founder-Match ideas, from which a founder can pick one up. Gate-3 (2026-07-02) resolves both prior [GAP]s in part: the list SPANS universities with a per-university filter (see gate-3 decision), and expressing interest NOTIFIES the idea's IP Manager who starts making connections (see gate-3 decision). [GAP: formal match completion — how the two-founder company forms after the IP Manager connects founder and professor — still TBD.]

decisions.title: Founder Match spans universities + per-university filter (gate-3)
decisions.detail: PO gate-3 decision (2026-07-02): the founder-facing Founder-Match browse list gets a FILTER control to filter ideas per university — and the list itself spans universities: founders see the published Founder-Match ideas ACROSS universities. This RESOLVES the previously flagged founder-visibility [GAP]: university isolation applies to IP Managers (who cannot see each other's IP), NOT to the founder-facing match list.

decisions.title: Founder interest notifies the IP Manager (gate-3)
decisions.detail: PO gate-3 decision (2026-07-02): when a founder expresses interest in a Founder-Match idea, that idea's IP Manager is NOTIFIED — so they can start making connections with that founder and get them connected to the professor. The IP Manager side gets a notification/inbox affordance ('new interest' items showing founder + idea) with the human-in-the-loop next step: the IP Manager connects founder <-> professor. Anything beyond that connect step (formal match completion, company formation) stays open — see the narrowed dependency.

decisions.title: IP Portfolio detail: company description (gate-3)
decisions.detail: PO gate-3 decision (2026-07-02): in the IP Manager's IP Portfolio, clicking a company/idea shows a spot with a DESCRIPTION of the company and what it does — an 'About this company / what it does' section on each portfolio entry's detail view.

decisions.title: IP Manager home = login landing page (gate-3)
decisions.detail: PO gate-3 decision (2026-07-02): CONFIRMED — the IP Manager role home IS the home page an IP Manager sees when they log in. This resolves the prior [GAP] on the feature's app placement for the IP Manager.

decisions.title: Wildfire Admin management tab
decisions.detail: PO gate-2 decision (2026-07-02, promoted from REC-2): the app gets a Wildfire Admin role/tab showing how the admin manages what universities are in the system, what's going through them (pipeline/volume per university), and who's attached to them (IP Managers, professors). Includes provisioning university orgs and assigning IP Managers.

decisions.title: Wildfire Admin mechanics + university drill-down (gate-3)
decisions.detail: PO gate-3 decision (2026-07-02): build out what the Wildfire Admin can DO — EDIT a university, REMOVE a university, REASSIGN an IP Manager, DEACTIVATE a university and/or people ('all that type of stuff'). The admin view shows which professors are tied to which university, and each university row is clickable (e.g. University of South Dakota) into a deeper, more robust university detail page: its IP Managers, professors, ideas/pipeline, status, and actions. Confirmation dialogs on destructive actions (remove/deactivate) are obvious rendering.

decisions.title: Multi-university tenancy — fully isolated organizations
decisions.detail: PO gate decision (2026-07-02, promoted from REC-4): each university is its own organization with its own IP Managers, fully isolated — an IP Manager cannot see other universities' IP, or the other universities at all. (Wildfire Admin sees all universities — gate-2.)

decisions.title: University IP is just an 'idea'
decisions.detail: IP is represented in the app as an idea, not a new object type. 'The research is just an idea in our world. It's not a separate thing. It's just an idea.'

decisions.title: Professor = Founder tag + university-IP-origin analytics tag
decisions.detail: The professor (idea owner) carries the existing Founder role/tag — there is no separate 'professor' role. PO gate decision (2026-07-02): additionally, a special analytics tag marks that this founder originated from a university IP idea. Even though the university owns the IP, the professor owns the idea and leads it.

decisions.title: New IP Manager role
decisions.detail: The person who manages the university's IP gets a new role. Their role title in the app is 'IP Manager' regardless of their university title (VP of research, IP office lead, etc.).

decisions.title: Not hackathon-only
decisions.detail: This is NOT solely for hackathons. Not all university IP is hackathon-appropriate (e.g. a device that makes a heart last longer wouldn't be built at a hackathon). Only a subset of ideas would go to a hackathon.

decisions.title: Private by default; Hold is the explicit deliberate disposition
decisions.detail: Imported IP goes in privately by default (private/unrouted). The IP Manager selects some or all and hits publish; publishing sends it out (e.g. to Founder Match), with a separate publish path to a hackathon. Gate-2 reconciliation (2026-07-02): the default state stays private/unrouted, and 'Hold' is now an explicit, deliberate disposition — marking an idea private to HOLD it in the app until the IP Manager figures out what to do with it — rather than private-by-default merely doubling as the hold state.

decisions.title: Import spreadsheet or add individually
decisions.detail: The IP Manager can import a spreadsheet of IP, or add IP individually with a button. Gate-2: an idea can be marked Hold (private) at import. [GAP: exact import/add mechanics not specified — 'however they want to do it'.]

decisions.title: Flag professor involvement per idea
decisions.detail: For each idea the IP Manager flags whether the professor wants to be a day-to-day co-founder OR is just a contact whom whoever takes the idea can reach out to directly. This reflects the two professor profiles.

decisions.title: Founder route reuses the existing process
decisions.detail: On the Founder route the professor is a Founder and runs through the Wildfire process exactly as founders do today; Founder Match brings a co-founder, resulting in two founders in one company, as currently set up.

decisions.title: Hackathon route = pickable idea only (no hackathon-management integration)
decisions.detail: On the Hackathon route the IP becomes a hackathon idea. Hackathon applicants can bring their own idea OR select a university IP idea to work on ('I like that one, I want to work on that one'). PO gate clarification (2026-07-02): this feature only marks/publishes an idea as hackathon-pickable — the separate hackathon-management system being built elsewhere is NOT integrated now; it will be updated later with these learnings (parked dependency).

decisions.title: Do NOT rethink founder role-gating now
decisions.detail: Today the only gated role is Founder (a user can be gated to Founder-only). The PO decided this is not the right time to rethink that gating model — leave it as is for this feature.

dependencies.detail: RESOLVED at PO gate (2026-07-02): one role — the VPR is merged into the IP Manager; no separate VPR role/tab. Kept here for traceability.

recommendations.title: Wire the university-IP idea into the existing Idea/Application + Founder Match machinery
recommendations.rationale: The PO says IP 'is just an idea' and that the Founder and Founder-Match routes reuse today's process. To FULLY serve the goal, the imported IP idea must actually connect to the existing idea/company entities and Founder Match rather than be a parallel silo.

recommendations.title: University-IP provenance label + professor contact on the idea
recommendations.rationale: Downstream founder-match users and hackathon participants need to know an idea is university-owned IP and who the professor contact is (especially for contact-only professors). Without provenance the 'reach out directly' path can't work.

recommendations.title: Private-vs-published state + empty state for the IP Manager's list
recommendations.rationale: The private-by-default/publish model needs a clear visible state per idea and a first-run empty state, or an IP Manager opening a fresh, empty list can't tell what's live vs held — the smallest thing that makes the publish model legible.

recommendations.title: Attribution / audit on import, routing, and publish
recommendations.rationale: Recording who imported, routed, and published each piece of IP protects the university relationship and is a cheap addition that a hand-built DoD would likely miss.

recommendations_resolved.title: Professor invite / account-provisioning flow
recommendations_resolved.resolution: ACCEPTED at PO gate 2 (2026-07-02) — promoted to decision 'Professor invite with Professor + linked-IP-idea tag': the IP Manager creates the professor's profile/account and sends the invite; a tag attaches them as a Professor with the IP idea they're working on, applied at account creation; the professor comes through the app the regular way.

recommendations_resolved.title: Super Admin provisioning of universities + assigning IP Managers

recommendations_resolved.title: Multi-university tenancy — each university its own org, IP Manager scoped to it
recommendations_resolved.resolution: ACCEPTED at PO gate (2026-07-02) — promoted to decision 'Multi-university tenancy — fully isolated organizations'.

role_tabs.title: IP Manager — Bring IP In, Route It & Track It
role_tabs.subtitle: The IP Manager (e.g. Kirby or Peter at USD) is the single university-side role (the VPR merged in at the PO gate): they decide to put the university's IP in the app, bring it in, associate each idea with its professor, create the professor's profile/account and send the invite, flag professor involvement, choose each piece of IP's disposition (four options), and track how every idea is doing on its route. Scoped to their own university only. Gate-3: their role home IS the home page they see when they log in (confirmed).

criteria.criterion: An IP Manager can bring IP into the app (spreadsheet import or individual add) and it lands private by default; an idea can be explicitly marked Hold at import.
Each imported idea is associated with a professor and carries the professor-involvement flag (co-founder vs contact).
From the idea, the IP Manager can create the professor's profile/account and send the invite; the account is created with a tag attaching them as a Professor linked to that IP idea.
An IP Manager can give each piece of IP exactly one disposition from four options (Founder / Hackathon / Founder Match / Hold).
An idea marked Hold stays private in the app (not visible downstream) until the IP Manager changes its disposition.
Publishing an idea moves it from private to the selected destination(s); unpublished IP is not visible downstream.

For each routed idea the IP Manager can see its current status on its route — founder-route progress through the Wildfire program, what was built at the hackathon, or how the founder match is doing — using the existing founder-tracking framework.
Clicking a company/idea in the IP Portfolio shows a description of the company and what it does (gate-3).

When a founder expresses interest in one of this university's Founder-Match ideas, the IP Manager sees a notification (founder + idea) and can start making connections — connecting the founder with the professor (gate-3; formal match completion stays TBD).
The IP Manager role home is the home page an IP Manager sees when they log in (gate-3).
A founder can have an account and log in to the app.

A logged-in founder sees a browsable list of ALL the published Founder-Match IP ideas ACROSS universities — the ideas submitted for other people to pick up; private/held/other-route ideas never appear (gate-3: the list spans universities).
The founder can filter the Founder-Match browse list per university (gate-3).

A founder can express interest in / pick up an idea from the list; expressing interest notifies the idea's IP Manager (gate-3). Formal match completion / company formation remains TBD — open dependency.
A Wildfire Admin can see and manage what universities are in the system, including provisioning a university org and assigning its IP Manager.
A Wildfire Admin can see what's going through each university — IP volume and disposition/publish breakdown per university.
A Wildfire Admin can see who's attached to each university — its IP Managers and professors — including which professors are tied to which university (gate-3).
A Wildfire Admin can edit a university, remove a university, reassign an IP Manager, and deactivate a university and/or people — with a confirmation step on destructive actions (gate-3).
Each university row is clickable into a deeper university detail page showing its IP Managers, professors, ideas/pipeline, status, and management actions (gate-3).
There is exactly one university-side role (IP Manager) — no separate VPR role or tab.

An IP Manager sees only their own university's organization and IP; other universities and their IP are completely invisible. (Wildfire Admin sees all universities. Gate-3: isolation applies to IP Managers, NOT to the founder-facing Founder-Match list, which spans universities.)
A professor who becomes a Founder from a university IP idea carries the special university-IP-origin analytics tag.
All IP data entry happens inside the Wildfire app by a logged-in user — no external data entry.
Existing app behavior (founders, mentors, hackathon roles) is unaffected.
Responsive web, mobile portrait supported. (Template default.)
